ai.description: This lizard reaches 40 cm in length. It is brownish-grey with a distinct white or yellow stripe along the lips and neck. A prominent crest of elongated scales runs along the nape and back.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Calotes mystaceus* is best distinguished by the prominent, creamy-white stripe extending from below the eye to the ear, which remains distinct even in non-breeding adults.
ai.habitat: The Indo-Chinese Forest Lizard inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically found in low-to-mid altitudes up to 1,500 meters within the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Indo-Chinese Forest Lizard is primarily diurnal and often displays a defensive strategy of freezing in place, relying on its cryptic coloration to blend into tree bark.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calotes mystaceus* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Calotes mystaceus* occurs in Northeast India, primarily in Assam, Mizoram, and Manipur, inhabiting lowland forests and foothills up to 1,000 meters elevation.
